newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Foreign firms may list in Singapore dlrs on SES - Hu.
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms may list in Singapore dlrs on SES - Hu.

text.p: Foreign companies listed in Singapore may convert their shares into Singapore-dollar denominated stocks, provided they meet some conditions, Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Tuesday.

"With immediate effect, foreign companies which meet the following criteria may apply to the MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) to convert or list their shares in Singapore dollar(s)," Hu said in a speech.
- The foreign company must be incorporated in Singapore and have at least two years operating track record there.
- The company must comply with the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) requirements governing the listing of foreign companies.
- The Singapore holding company should already be approved under the operational headquarters (OHQ) or finance and treasury (FTC) scheme.
- Activities conducted by the OHQ or FTC must be sufficiently substantial to qualify it for at least 10-year OHQ or FTC award.
- The senior management responsible for managing the business of the listed company must be located in Singapore.
- The listed company must have more than 35 percent of revenue, profits or expenses attributable to its Singapore operations.

Hu said those companies meeting these conditions would also be permitted to issue Singapore dollar bonds under what he called "suitable conditions where the majority of the proceeds raised is used for their Singapore operations."
"Foreign companies which meet these criteria, may apply to MAS through the SES to list their shares in Singapore dollar(s)," he said.
